title: Pause, verify, and protect
summary: A short routine for slowing down a pressured request.

sections.heading: Pause
sections.body: Stop the requested action and avoid replying through the same channel.

sections.heading: Verify
sections.body: Use a trusted contact method you already know, not a destination supplied by the message.

sections.heading: Protect
sections.body: Do not share passwords, PINs, one-time codes, or recovery phrases.

knowledge_checks.question: A caller says you must act immediately. What is the safest first step?
options: Pause and verify through a known channel
Share the code so the account is not closed
Forward the message to several contacts
knowledge_checks.explanation: Pressure is a reason to slow down. Do not use contact details supplied by the unexpected request.

title: Recovery basics
summary: Steps to take when an account, payment, or device may be affected.

sections.heading: Contain
sections.body: Stop further interaction, secure the affected account, and contact the relevant provider through a known channel.

sections.heading: Record
sections.body: Keep dates, messages, receipts, and account notices without forwarding sensitive secrets.

sections.heading: Report
sections.body: Use an independently located official reporting path when one has been verified.

knowledge_checks.question: What should you preserve after a suspicious payment or account request?
options: Messages, dates, receipts, and transaction references
A forwarded copy containing a one-time code
knowledge_checks.explanation: Preserve useful records while keeping passwords, PINs, and one-time codes private.
